items.stem: You prompt a model to document an API from its signatures and notes. What most protects accuracy?

options.text: Ground the draft in the provided signatures and notes and verify claims against the code
options.rationale: Correct: grounding plus verification keeps the docs faithful to real behaviour.

options.text: Let the model describe how the API probably behaves
Ask only for a longer document
Skip the notes and rely on the model's training data
options.rationale: Ignoring the source causes drift from reality.

items.explanation: Correct: grounding plus verification keeps the docs faithful to real behaviour.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices make AI code refactoring safer? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Require that the refactor preserve existing behaviour and back it with tests
options.rationale: Correct: behaviour-preserving refactors verified by tests are safer.

options.text: Review the generated diff before merging
options.rationale: Correct: human review catches issues the model introduces.

options.text: Merge immediately if the code looks plausible
Delete the existing tests to avoid conflicts

items.explanation: Correct: behaviour-preserving refactors verified by tests are safer.

items.stem: A generated explanation of a function reads clearly and fluently. What should you do?

options.text: Check it against the function's actual behaviour before trusting it
options.rationale: Correct: fluent prose can still misdescribe what the code does.

options.text: Publish it because it reads well

items.explanation: Correct: fluent prose can still misdescribe what the code does.
